# Voicing and voice leading

Pitches are MIDI numbers, 60 = middle C. Onsets are slots 0 to 15 of a sixteenth grid, so slot 4 is beat 2; lengths are in beats. Tiers: M1 is needed in a first test set, M2 has one or two sources or is a jazz or world idiom, M3 is single-source, inferred or theory only. Tags: `source states`, `measured`, `derived` (our computation on public data), `inferred` (our reading), `snippet` (a search excerpt), `single source`, `proposal` (a policy, not a fact). Source ids are listed in `dictionary/sources.json`.

## Voicings

| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| close | `voicing.close` | close; span at most 12; gap at most 4 | All tones sit within one octave, and no two neighbouring tones are more than four semitones apart. | M1 | source states | guides |
| open, sense `voicing`, default | `voicing.open.voicing` | open; span at least 13; gap at least 5 | Tones spread out: some neighbours are five or more semitones apart, or the whole chord spans more than an octave. Either condition counts. | M1 | inferred | guides, lexicon |
| open, sense `fifths` | `voicing.open.fifths` | quintal; step 7; notes at least 2; notes at most 4 | Tones stacked in fifths with no third, so the chord sounds hollow and wide. It is common in film writing. | M2 | source states | guides |
| open, sense `guitar-chord` | `voicing.open.guitar-chord` | open; notes at least 4; notes at most 6; lowest 40 | A chord shaped like a guitar open-string chord: four to six tones, none below the low open string at 40. | M3 | proposal | lexicon |

| drop-2 | `voicing.drop-2` | drop-2; span at most 16; span at least 15; drop voices 2 from the top | Take a close voicing and lower its second voice from the top by an octave. Four notes then span 15 or 16 semitones, and a triad lowers its middle voice. | M1 | source states | guides |
| shell (shell voicing), sense `root-3rd-7th`, default | `voicing.shell.root-3rd-7th` | shell; notes at least 3; notes at most 3; bass root; degrees 1 3 7 from the bottom | Only the root, third and seventh of a seventh chord. The fifth is left out. | M1 | source states | guides |
| shell, sense `root-and-named` | `voicing.shell.root-and-named` | shell; notes at least 2; notes at most 2; bass root; degrees 1 from the bottom | For a triad, the root plus one named note such as the third or fifth. This is the second reading of the word. | M1 | source states | guides |
| rootless, sense `type-a`, default | `voicing.rootless.type-a` | rootless-a; degrees 3 5 7 9 from the bottom | Leave the root to the bass and play the third, fifth, seventh and ninth from the bottom up, near middle C. Cmaj9 becomes 64 67 71 74. | M1 | source states | guides |
| rootless, sense `type-b` | `voicing.rootless.type-b` | rootless-b; degrees 7 9 3 5 from the bottom | Leave the root to the bass and play the seventh, ninth, third and fifth from the bottom up, near middle C. Cmaj9 becomes 59 62 64 67. | M1 | source states | guides |

| pad floor | `voicing.pad-floor` | muddy; tones under 51; at most under it 0 | Pads and wide chords stay above a high-pass near 150 Hz, which is MIDI note 50.37, so the lowest tone is 51 or higher. | M1 | source states | guides |
| drop-3 | `voicing.drop-3` | drop-3; notes at least 4; drop voices 3 from the top | Take a close voicing and lower its third voice from the top by an octave. | M2 | source states | guides |

The root plays alone low, neighbouring voices move at most three semitones, and each chord lasts a bar or more. | M2 | source states | guides |
| lush | `voicing.lush` | lush; span at least 16; pitch classes at least 5 | A full chord of at least five pitch classes spanning 16 semitones or more, sustained into the next chord. | M2 | inferred | lexicon |
| wide | `voicing.wide` | wide; span at least 19; gap at least 5; bass root | A span of 19 semitones or more, with the root alone in the bass and upper voices five or more semitones apart. Stereo width is a preset matter. | M2 | source states | guides |
| muddy | `voicing.muddy` | muddy; tones under 48; at most under it 2 | A voicing is muddy when a pair of tones lies below its floor in the low-interval table, or when three tones sit below 48. The rule holds the clean side: at most two tones below 48. | M2 | source states | guides |

## Voice leading

| Word | Id | Rule | Meaning | Tier | Tag | Sources |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| common tone | `voice-leading.common-tone` | common-tone | A tone shared by two neighbouring chords keeps the same MIDI note instead of jumping an octave. | M1 | source states | guides |
| nearest tone | `voice-leading.nearest-tone` | nearest-tone; leap at most 4 | Each upper voice moves to the nearest tone of the next chord, by one or two semitones where possible. A leap over four is flagged, and the bass may leap. | M1 | source states | guides |
| smallest motion | `voice-leading.smallest-motion` | smallest-motion | Choose the octave placement of the next chord so the voices travel the least in total. For three sorted voices in MIDI 48 to 84, a cyclic C-G-Am-F loop totals 12. | M2 | derived | guides, lexicon |
| no parallels | `voice-leading.no-parallels` | no-parallels | No two voices move in parallel fifths or octaves. Rock, power chords, planing and trap allow them. | M2 | source states | guides |
| top hold | `voice-leading.top-hold` | top-hold | The top note stays put while the inner voices change underneath it. | M3 | source states | guides |
| planing | `voice-leading.planing` | planing | Every voice moves by the same interval, so the chord shape slides in parallel. | M2 | source states | guides |
| loop return | `voice-leading.loop-return` | loop-return; leap at most 4 | The last chord of a loop leaves its lowest note within four semitones of the first chord's lowest note, so the loop turns over smoothly. | M3 | inferred | lexicon |
